αὐτήν: αὐτός — self; intensive/personal pron., fem. acc. sg.: ’her, it’
βροτοῖσιν: βροτός — mortal, mortal man; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οῖς)
γενοίατο: γίγνομαι — become; aor. opt. 3 pl., epic -ατο (= Attic γένοιντο): ’would become’
γερήνιος: Γερήνιος — Gerenian (standing epithet of Nestor); masc. nom. sg.; meaning uncertain — perhaps from Gerenia/Gerenon in Messenia, or linked to γέρων ’old man’ or γέρας ’honour’
γνώμεναι: γιγνώσκω — come to know, recognize; epic inf. in -μεναι: ’to be known’
γνώσεαι: γιγνώσκω — come to know, perceive; fut. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic γνώσῃ)
δεινὰ: δεινός — fearful, terrible; neut. nom. pl., agreeing with ῥέεθρα
δεκάτῳ: δέκατος — tenth; masc./neut. dat. sg., dat. of time: ’in the tenth (year)’
δηρόν: δηρός — long, lasting; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’for long, for a long time’
δράκων: δράκων — serpent, snake; masc. nom. sg.
δυνάμεσθα: δύναμαι — be able, can; epic pres. opt. 1 pl. (= Attic δυναίμεθα): with κεν ’we could’ · also pres. indic. 1 pl., epic -μεσθα (= Attic δυνάμεθα): ’we were able’ (+ inf.)
εἰδομένη: εἴδομαι — seem, make oneself like, appear as (+ dat.); pres. part. fem. nom. sg. · also functioning as aor. part. (the same -όμενος form serves both in Homer), ’having made herself like’ (Μέντορι εἰδομένη)
εὑρέμεναι: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. inf. act., epic -έμεναι (= Attic εὑρεῖν)
θέμεναι: τίθημι — put, place, set; aor. inf. act., epic -έμεναι (= Attic θεῖναι)
θανάτοιο: θάνατος — death; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θείοιο: θεῖος — divine, godlike; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεσπεσίῃ: θεσπέσιος — wondrous, prodigious, superhuman in scale; fem. dat. sg. (ἠχῇ θεσπεσίῃ ’with a wondrous outcry’)
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’) · also of a goddess (θεός is common gender) · also nom. sg. subject, of a god already introduced by epithets but not yet named: ’the god’ · also nom. sg. in apposition to a name following: θεὸς … Ἑρμείας ’a god, Hermes’
θῆκεν: τίθημι — put, place; aor. 3 sg. · also ’make (someone a certain way)’, with double acc.: ’made him (taller)’
κακότητι: κακότης — badness, misery, distress; fem. dat. sg.
κακὰ: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κακὰ ἔργα ’bad deeds’
κακὸς: κακός — bad, base, cowardly; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’base’ · also masc. nom. sg., attributive with a noun: ’evil’ (κακὸς δαίμων ’an evil power’) · also masc. nom. sg. as a substantive, subject: ’a base man’ (κακὸς κακὸν ἡγηλάζει)
κατήσθιε: κατεσθίω — eat up, devour; impf. 3 sg., without movable ν (= κατήσθιεν): ’was devouring’
κενεόν: κενεός — empty; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic κενόν): ’empty’, ’empty-handed’
κεῖνος: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. nom. sg.
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κομόωντες: κομάω — wear the hair long; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic κομῶντες): ’long-haired’
κρήνην: κρήνη — spring, fountain; fem. acc. sg.
κῆρα: κήρ — doom, fate of death; fem. acc. sg.
κῆρες: κήρ — death-spirit, doom of death; fem. nom. pl.: ’the death-spirits’ (a different word from κῆρ ’heart’)
λᾶαν: λᾶας — stone, rock; masc. acc. sg. (Attic λίθος)
μέλει: μέλω — be a care, be an object of concern (impersonal, + dat. of the person, nom. of the thing); pres. 3 sg.
μήδεά: μῆδος — plan, counsel; in the pl. also the genitals; neut. acc. pl. (accent from the following enclitic)
μίμνετε: μίμνω — stay, remain (= Attic μένω); pres. imper. 2 pl.: ’stay!’
μετέειπε: μετεῖπον — speak among, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic μετεῖπε)
μῆνα: μείς, μήν — month; masc. acc. sg., acc. of duration: ’for a month’
μῆχος: μῆχος — means, remedy; neut. nom./acc. sg.
νῆες: ναῦς — ship; fem. nom. pl., epic νῆες
οὓς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. acc. pl.
οὗτος: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; masc. nom. sg.
πέλωρα: πέλωρον (πέλωρ) — monster, monstrous thing; neut. acc. pl.
παισὶν: παῖς — child, son; masc. dat. pl.: ’to children’
πρόσθ: πρόσθε — before, in front of; prep. + gen., elided (πρόσθ’ = πρόσθε) · also adv., ’ahead, in front’ (πρόσθ’ ἡγεμόνευεν ’led the way in front’)
πτολίπορθος: πτολίπορθος — city-sacking, sacker of cities; masc. nom. sg., epithet of Odysseus
πόνος: πόνος — toil, labour, hardship; masc. nom. sg.
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.
πὰρ: παρά (apocope πάρ, functioning as an adverb) — beside, alongside; adv. · also a preposition + acc., ’beside’ (πὰρ Νέστορα) · also preverb in tmesis (πὰρ … θῆκεν = παρέθηκε ’set before’) · also a preposition + dat., ’beside’ (πὰρ πυρί ’beside the fire’) · also a preposition + gen., ’from (the side of)’ (πὰρ Ταφίων ’from the Taphians’) · also a preposition + dat., ’among, in the company of’ (πὰρ παύροισι ’among few’)
πῇ: πῇ — where?, to what place?; interrog. adv.
σήματα: σῆμα — sign, mark, marker; neut. acc. pl.
σμερδαλέον: σμερδαλέος — terrible, dreadful; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’terribly’
σμερδαλέος: σμερδαλέος — terrible, dread, fearsome; masc. nom. sg.
στείχοντες: στείχω — go, walk; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’going’
σφέας: σφεῖς — they; pron., masc. acc. pl., epic σφέας (= Attic σφᾶς), governed by διά: ’through them’ · also acc. pl. object of a verb of teaching: ’them’ (σφέας … ἐδίδαξε ’taught them’) · also acc. pl. reflexive object, with αὐτούς: ’themselves’ (πυκάζοιεν σφέας αὐτούς) · also acc. pl. direct object: ’them’ (Ζεὺς σφέας τίσαιτο ’may Zeus punish them’) · also acc. pl. object of a compound verb of coming: ’them’ (σφέας εἰσαφίκηται ’comes to them’) · also acc. pl. subject of an infinitive: ’them (to be)’ (σφέας … ἔμμεναι)
σῆμα: σῆμα — mark, sign; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’sign’ (τόδε σῆμα τετύχθω ’let this sign be made’)
τέρας: τέρας — sign, portent, marvel; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’a portent’ (τέρας ἄλλο φανήτω ’let another portent appear’)
τίσασθαι: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay, requite; mid. exact vengeance, punish; aor. inf. mid. τίσασθαι: ’to take vengeance on’, same root as ἐτίσατο in this part
τελεῖται: τελέω — bring to pass, fulfil, accomplish; pres. pass. 3 sg.
τοί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl. ’they’ · also relative: ’who’ · also encl. dat. sg. pron. σύ ’to you’ (= τοι, accented before a following enclitic, e.g. τοί τι) · also τοι, the affirming particle, accented τοί before an enclitic: ἀλλ’ ἦ τοί σε ’but truly you’
τούσδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this; demonstrative pron., masc. acc. pl.
τὼς: τώς — thus, so; epic adv. (= Attic οὕτως)
φάσαν: φημί — say; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔφασαν): ’they said’
φέροντες: φέρω — carry, bear; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
φέρουσαι: φέρω — carry, bear; pres. part. act. fem. nom. pl., agreeing with κῆρες: ’bearing’
φαίνων: φαίνω — show, bring to light; pres. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’showing’
φόνον: φόνος — murder, slaughter, bloodshed; masc. acc. sg.
φῦλα: φῦλον — tribe, race; neut. nom. pl.
χρόνον: χρόνος — time; masc. acc. sg., acc. of duration
ψεῦδος: ψεῦδος — falsehood, lie; neut. acc. sg.
ἀγλαὸν: ἀγλαός — splendid, radiant, bright; masc./neut. acc. sg.
ἀκροτάτῳ: ἄκρος — topmost, outermost; superlative ἀκρότατος, masc. dat. sg.
ἀλλήλοισιν: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
ἀλόχοιο: ἄλοχος — wife, bedfellow; fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀνώγει: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., + inf.: ’was bidding’ · also pres. 3 sg., a present formed on the perf. stem: ’bids’ (ἐποτρύνει καὶ ἀνώγει ’urges and bids’)
ἀσχαλάᾳ: ἀσχαλάω — be distressed, chafe, be vexed; pres. 3 sg. act., epic diectasis (= Attic ἀσχαλᾷ)
ἄελλαι: ἄελλα — storm, squall, gust; fem. nom. pl.
ἄνεῳ: ἄνεως — silent, speechless; masc. nom. pl.
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἐθέλουσιν: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. 3 pl., ν-movable
ἐκτελέουσιν: ἐκτελέω — bring to completion, accomplish; pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἐκτελοῦσιν)
ἐναίσιμα: ἐναίσιμος — fitting, in due measure, true (of an omen); neut. acc. pl.
ἐοικότες: ἔοικα — be like, be fitting, resemble; perf. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’fitting’ (μῦθοι ἐοικότες ’fitting words’) · also + dat., ’like, resembling’ (ἄνδρεσσιν ἐοικότες ’like men’)
ἐπίσπῃ: ἐφέπω — come upon, meet with, pursue; aor. subj. 3 sg., epic ἐπίσπῃ: ’meets with’
ἐριδαίνομεν: ἐριδαίνω — strive, vie, contend; pres. 1 pl.
ἐσθλὸς: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; masc. nom. sg.
ἐτεὸν: ἐτεός — true, real; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’truly, in truth’
ἐφάνη: φαίνω — show; aor. pass. 3 sg., augmented (beside unaugmented φάνη): ’appeared’
ἑσταότες: ἵστημι — set up; perf. stand; perf. part. masc. nom. pl., epic ἑσταότες (= Attic ἑστῶτες)
ἔβαινον: βαίνω — go, step; impf. 3 pl. (or 1 sg.), augmented; in tmesis with ἀνά (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’they mounted’)
ἔθ: ἔτι — still, yet; adv., elided ἔθ’ before a rough breathing (with negative: ’no longer’)
ἔφηνε: φαίνω — show, make appear; aor. 3 sg. act.: ’showed, sent as a sign’
ἕνα: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one; masc. acc. sg. (ἕνα θυμόν ’one mind’)
ἠγερέθοντο: ἀγείρω — gather, assemble; impf. pass. 3 pl., epic -εθ- formation (= Attic ἠγείροντο)
ἱπποβότοιο: ἱππόβοτος — horse-pasturing, grazed by horses; adj., neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου) · also gen. of comparison after ἐπήρατος, of an implied land (fem.): μᾶλλον ἐπήρατος ἱπποβότοιο ’lovelier than a horse-pastured land’ · also fem. gen. sg., agreeing with a place-name: ’horse-pasturing’ (Ἤλιδος ἱπποβότοιο ’horse-pasturing Elis’)
ἱππότα: ἱππότης — horseman, charioteer (epithet of Nestor); masc. nom. sg., old form in short -α
ὀδυρομένη: ὀδύρομαι — lament, mourn for; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀλεῖται: ὄλλυμι — destroy; mid. perish; fut. 3 sg. mid., contracted (ὀλέεται): ’will perish’
ὅθεν: ὅθεν — from where, whence; relative adv.
ὅου: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc./neut. gen. sg., epic (ὅου = Attic οὗ)
ὕδωρ: ὕδωρ — water; neut. acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb (ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ ‘wind and current’)
